## Overview

Every year each state reports to the Federal Highway Administration what its highway agency spent on capital projects, and what kind of work the money paid for. This project pulls those reports for 2012 to 2023 and asks a simple question: how much of it goes to repaving and repairing the roads that already exist?

The reports do not single out resurfacing. Most states fold it into a broader line, so the measure here is FHWA's "3R" group: resurfacing, restoration, rehabilitation, and minor widening.

## Key Findings

- States spent \$29\.2 billion on 3R work in 2023, up from \$18\.0 billion in 2012. That is a 63% rise before inflation.
- 3R work took 31% of state highway capital spending in 2023, against 27% in 2012. The share peaked at 33% in 2020.
- It is the largest single use of the money, ahead of new roads and added capacity.

## Reading the Numbers

- **Dollars are not adjusted for inflation.** Construction costs rose over these years, so the increase in dollars overstates the increase in work done. The share of spending is not affected.
- **State agencies only.** What cities and counties spend on their own streets is not in these reports.
- **Local-class roads are left out.** They only appear in the table from 2015, so they are dropped to keep every year comparable.
- **Reused figures.** When a state does not report, FHWA carries its previous year's numbers forward.

## Data and Code

The source is FHWA Highway Statistics, Table SF-12A, one workbook per year. The [data notebook](road-paving.ipynb) downloads the workbooks, reads every sheet, and checks each column against the totals FHWA publishes before any figure is used.

The code is on [GitHub](https://github.com/eschnitger/eschnitger.github.io/tree/main/projects/road-paving).
